rv.q: Yes, this is a huge concert — not a full production.

The runaway cart is also excised; that quickie scene happens on one of the massive video screens atop the Radio City stage. There’s not even a song list in the program. But if you’re here, you probably know every Boublil-Schönberg-Kretzmer number by heart.

Producer Cameron Mackintosh reconfigured the show for a world tour celebrating its 40th anniversary with what he’s calling The Arena Concert Spectacular. But this is no mere concert: it is performed in costume with enough technical razzle dazzle to make the experience every bit as satisfying as the fully staged productions of the past.
Between a cast of vocal powerhouses and sound design that turns Radio City into a cathedral, it's easy to forgive the clunky visuals and just let the score of Les Misérables take over.

cn.t: Critics praise this arena adaptation of the beloved musical, with reviewers celebrating its anthemic score and grand spectacle that honors the enduring power of Hugo's story nearly a decade after leaving Broadway.
